newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index trade mixed, some see range.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index trade mixed, some see range.

text.p: Trading in major U.S. stock index options was mixed Tuesday, and some dealers expect the market to hold to a trading range for the near term.
"There is a lot of local trading both ways," one S&P 500 index futures-options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said. "It's repositioning, basically.
"This is a trading range situation," he added.
The stock market was rebounding from Monday's decline, led by the Dow industrial average, which added 65 points to 7,924 after dropping 37 on Monday.
The S&P 500 index rose 5 to 917.20 and September S&P 500 futures, which fell 9.40 Monday, gained 7.40 to 925.75.
"Everyone thinks this market is not moving" this week, the futures-options trader said.
But Jay Shartsis, head of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co, noted that the index put/call ratio was fairly low by midday Tuesday, suggesting investors still expected further gains.

He noted data from the Hirsch Organization's Stock Trader's Almanac that showed the first few days of July typically are strong but are followed by a mixed to lower trend that resolves itself to the upside by month end.
The Almanac also shows that the Dow closed higher every July from 1989 through 1995. Last July, the bellwether average fell about 126 points, or 2.2 percent.
Shartsis said the market's steady rally over the last couple of years has made some technical indicators, including the put/call ratio, less dependable.
"Over the last couple of years we've had, during several peariods, very bearish technical evidence," he said. "And on many of those occasions, the market didn't respond to it and continued on up."
He said the pattern has caused investors, traders and analysts to disregard "bearish" technical indicators.
"So at the ultimate top -- and I guess there will be one some day -- how would you ever recognize it, since evidence has been shown to be unreliable?"
"It's setting up a very interesting dilemma," he said.
